correctness.rationale: A fresh complete enumeration of all 1296 labelled profiles and three perfect matchings reproduces labelled counts 48/1098/150 and canonical orbit counts 2/51/7. The frozen verifier independently cross-checks stability in two implementations and verifies the same result by Burnside fixed-point counting, including orbit sizes and both unsolvable representatives.

evidence: Mertens determines solvability probability; Irving gives the general algorithm; OEIS counts all orbits.

evidence: Knowing 48 unsolvable labelled profiles and 60 total orbits cannot determine the number of unsolvable orbits or one-versus-two stable matching classes.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The complete group-action refinement is additional.

evidence: There are 1296 labelled strict profiles and 60 simultaneous-relabeling orbits. The submitted theorem stratifies the orbits by number of stable matchings and stabilizer size.

evidence: A356584 gives 60 orbits; A358648 gives 1296 labelled profiles; no checked table gives 2,51,7.

originality.rationale: Mertens gives exact small-n solvability probabilities, and OEIS A356584 gives the total orbit count 60 at four agents; these account for coarse marginals but not the stability-count split 2/51/7, orbit-size refinement, or the statement that the 48 labelled unsolvable profiles form exactly two isomorphism classes. Resultary returned no covering theorem.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, software table or course note may contain the same four-agent stability refinement.

value.rationale: Four agents are the smallest nontrivial even size with unsolvable stable-roommates instances; the complete stability-stratified orbit census is a natural exact boundary classification and useful algorithmic benchmark.
residual_risks: An unindexed thesis, software table or course note may contain the same four-agent stability refinement.

final_claim: The 60 strict four-person stable-roommates isomorphism classes split as 2 with no stable matching, 51 with exactly one and 7 with exactly two, with the stated orbit-size refinement; the two unsolvable classes are the two orientations of the classical cyclic obstruction.
scientific_limitations: An unindexed thesis, software table or course note may contain the same four-agent stability refinement.
